Naomi — quick notes from pricing: 40% across the board is above our standard authorized band for AEs. We can consider a structured bridge instead:
- Option A (preferred): 25% off list for the first 2 months + usage-based credits (cap $15k) if we hit agreed milestones.
- Option B: 35% off for first month only, revert to published published pilot rates thereafter.

Guardrails I want in SOW: explicit pilot end date (90 days), clear conversion terms to Dedicated with an uplift clause, and a maximum aggregate discount cap for the account (so seat/usage add-ons don't stack discounts). We'll also require a signed purchase order (PO) that acknowledges the time-limited nature.

If we pursue Option A we'll need written VP/CFO approval because the revenue impact exceeds our delegation. Happy to run numbers with Finance.

Kimberly / Naomi — I've modeled both options against our unit economics given a Private VPC deployment (higher infra baseline). Assumptions: pilot-month tokens 4M, post-pilot committed 6 months @ 6M/month. Key takeaways:
- Option A (25% + $15k credits) reduces short-term margin but keeps ARPU when they convert. NPV over 12 months still positive assuming conversion rate >= 70%.
- Option B (35% for 1 month) protects margin but may be insufficient to unblock procurement quickly.

Recommendation: Approve Option A with two additional conditions: 1) PO + signed SOW before discount window starts; 2) an automatic step-change to a minimum committed monthly spend if conversion happens within 90 days (pre-agreed uplift). That preserves conversion economics and limits exposure.

I've attached a compact model (spreadsheet) to the thread.
